snapshot_face_sync_closeout.question: why the published snapshot did not appear to update on the daily runtime
snapshot_face_sync_closeout.finding: The published snapshot itself was already re-frozen on every converge (snapshot_version carries the candidate SHA and refreshes.changed=true). What did not follow were (a) the served code/rendering face and (b) the consumer of the snapshot. Four layered causes were proven: 1) the published face (sc.edition.release.snapshot, which the navigation release gate reads) was released by a lane independent of the code face, so a contract change could be deployed while the gate kept reading the previous contract - fixed by making daily.runtime.candidate.release order bundle_sync -> source_revision.align -> published_face.converge; 2) SC_SOURCE_REVISION stayed at the previous commit, so /api/runtime-version reported a stale served revision even though the tree was updated - fixed by declaring the exact deployed HEAD in the same entry; 3) the face freeze must upgrade the projection module, but guard.codex.fast.upgrade rejected the undeclared upgrade, so the freeze never made the new projection code live - fixed by declaring CODEX_NEED_UPGRADE=1 with CODEX_MODULES and carrying the upgrade tail into the failure message; 4) the canonical projection (server) and its frontend mirror indexed only action_id>0 / menu_containers and rejected the contract-declared scene entry (menu_id 1004, action_id 0), which made every system.init for the locked role return HTTP 500 while the guard reported PASS - fixed by consuming the same declared authority carrier end to end, with the release-gate guard extended to mirror the projection tail.
